spp_donkey.text: Guernsey folk are called donkeys, ânes. Some say because the streets are steep, some say we're stubborn. I say it's both and it's a compliment.
Jersey has the crapauds, the toads. Sark has the crows. Alderney has the rabbits. We've all got a name, and we've all pretended not to mind.

spp_gache_lady.text: Gâche. Not 'gash', not 'gosh', with a long a, as in 'gâch'. Fruit loaf with butter, made by the oven-load on Sunday and eaten by Wednesday.
The Guernsey bean jar is a different thing entirely. Beans, pork, a trotter, hours in the baker's oven. If you can smell it at nine in the morning, someone's on the right track.

spp_hugo_fan.text: Victor Hugo spent fifteen years here and wrote about Guernsey as if he owned it. Les Misérables came out in 1862, and he wrote much of it here. Toilers of the Sea followed in 1866, set round these very rocks.
He gave a Christmas dinner every year for poor children, and he wrote standing up, at a desk in a glass room at the top of the house.

spp_sailor_sark.text: Sark? Pretty little island. No cars, no street lights, a very big sky. Hop aboard.

spp_sailor_poole.text: Back to Poole? The Bailiwick Belle leaves when the tide agrees. It's a good crossing, mostly. Hold your hat.

spp_sailor_jersey.text: St Helier? Jersey's just over the horizon, with the crapauds and the cows. They're good people, for a toad.

st_peter_port_bureau.text: Guernsey pounds are at par with sterling. Shops here take your English money, but we pay out in Guernsey notes, and the mainland won't touch those.
